correctness.rationale: For F_p(z)=(2/pi)K(sqrt(z))/(p-(1/2)Log(1-z)), the elliptic ODE and the Frobenius expansion K=C0+t(C0-1)/4+O(t²log t) yield at p0=log 4 a cut-jump -u/[4D_p0(u)] and derivative jump 1/D_p(u)+lower order, D_p(u)=(p-(1/2)log u)²+pi²/4. The pole 1-e^(2p) stays outside the unit disk uniformly in p near p0. Laplace substitution u=v/n gives a_n(p0)~ -1/[pi n²(log n)²] and derivative ~4/[pi n(log n)²] uniformly on J. FTC at p0+lambda/n proves the 4lambda-1 transition, strict increasing local degree-n curves, zero p_n=p0+1/(4n)+o(1/n), and N(delta)~1/(4delta), using Deng-Kou-Zhong endpoint negativity for finitely many indices. I independently implemented the exact Taylor recurrence and derivative at 75-digit precision: degree 30/60/120/240 roots yield n*(p_n-p0)=0.3142083,0.3096062,0.3055894,0.3020333. The finite tests are not proof of the uniform contour estimates.

originality.rationale: Endpoint sign at p0 and endpoint coefficient decay are pre-existing. The parameter derivative uniformity and first-positive-degree scaling jointly quantify the onset beyond endpoint monotonicity; Tian-Yang parameter-range criteria do not state the critical degree. Full Deng preprint and 2022 paper bodies were inaccessible, so only their inspected abstracts/preview support the limited comparison.

value.rationale: The first failed Taylor coefficient is a natural sharp quantitative refinement of an established absolute-monotonicity endpoint. The reciprocal perturbation cutoff and universal linear boundary-layer transition supply a nontrivial stability scale needed to understand finite Taylor truncations.
